questions.q: Why is nature called our science laboratory?
questions.a: Every field, pond and sky offers materials and phenomena to observe and test.

questions.q: Give one observation from nature that leads to a science question.
questions.a: Ants follow a line - why? Observing leads to questions about how they communicate.

questions.q: How should we treat nature while learning from it?
questions.a: Observe without harming - do not pluck, catch or disturb more than needed.

questions.q: How can litmus or turmeric tell acids from bases?
questions.a: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue and turmeric reddish-brown.

questions.q: Name two acidic and two basic substances found at home.
questions.a: Acidic: lemon juice, vinegar. Basic: soap solution, baking soda.

questions.q: What are neutral substances? Give an example.
questions.a: Substances that are neither acidic nor basic, like water or sugar solution.

questions.q: How is a turmeric indicator prepared and used?
questions.a: Rub turmeric on paper, dry it; a base turns the stain red, acids leave it yellow.

questions.q: Name a natural indicator other than litmus.
questions.a: Turmeric, red cabbage juice or China rose (hibiscus) petals.
Acids and bases are often colourless - indicators reveal which is which.

questions.q: How does an antacid relieve indigestion?
questions.a: The mild base neutralises excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

questions.q: Why is slaked lime added to acidic soil?
questions.a: The base neutralises the soil's acidity so crops grow better.

questions.q: What neutralises an ant bite (formic acid) on the skin?
questions.a: A mild base like baking soda paste (or calamine lotion).
